result:
I changed nothing this run. CPU is the bottleneck, and the one adjustment that would help needs a scheduler restart that isn't safe yet. I also found that the scheduler log has been hiding FEBio failures, including one I wrongly reported as clean at 12:00.

**Current state**
- **Old FEBio queue:** 9 runs going (5 long physrotFr, 4 short physrotG5), 8 short G1/G2 jobs waiting (oldest 17 min). The waiting jobs should clear in about 40 min. 7 / 8 / 5 / 7 runs finished in hours 09 / 10 / 11 / 12.
- **CPU:** 27.3 of 32 quota cores used, 13 % of periods throttled. No two runs share a core.
- **Memory and disk:** 23 GB in use (the rest of the 137 GB is page cache), no new out-of-memory kills; /raid has 668 GB free.
- **GPUs:** GPU3 has been empty all day, but that isn't costing anything: every run is limited by CPU, not GPU.
- **Health:** every FEBio log was written in the last 6 s, and all tmux services are up.
- **New task queue:** still idle since 10-28, with 5 failed gate2 tasks.

**Why no change:** a 10th run (`CPU_OVERCOMMIT` 1.125 → 1.25) would add about 2 cores, but it needs a `biocage_sched` restart. That would wrongly mark the CPU split run physrotFr_p125 as ended and could start a duplicate in the same directory. p125 has 4 of 6 sub-cases done, so roughly 30–60 min left. Next run: if p125 has finished and at least 3 jobs are waiting, I'll raise it and measure before and after.

**Failures the scheduler log hides:** `scheduler.log` records the wrapper's exit code, not FEBio's.
- physrotFr_p084 ended in FEBio ERROR TERMINATION (2 negative jacobians, failed to converge at t = 3.048), yet the log says exit=0.
- physrotFr_p109's extension and flexion sub-cases also ended in ERROR; the run itself is still going.
- Across today, 31 of 90 run records show an abnormal end, and the log shows none of them. Some physrotS ones date from this morning's full-disk and restart incidents. I didn't check which of the rest were superseded by later series.

These look like physics outcomes, so I did not requeue anything.

**Needs a person**
- The science roles should decide what to do about p084 and p109.
- Scheduler fixes (outside my scope):
  - log FEBio's own result in the "finished" line;
  - recognise CPU split runs when it restarts;
  - stop new runs from taking cores already used by older runs.
- Queue the next work: after the G jobs, only the long physrotFr runs remain.
- Decide on the 5 failed gate2 tasks and on physrot2_p001 / zz_mc_c0.1_tied.

I wrote the report, status.json and one line in `foreman_actions.log`, and saved a memory note so later runs count failures from the run records instead of the scheduler log.

Files are in `work/agents/foreman/`:
- report_20261031_1257.md
- status.json
